extracted.mesh_code:
real L = 1.0;    // normalized design-domain width
real H = 1.0;    // normalized design-domain height
real lq = 0.2;   // half-length of the chip heat-flux segment (chip = central 40%)
border C01(t=0, L/2-lq){x=t; y=0; label=1;}         // bottom edge, adiabatic left
border C02(t=0, 2*lq){x=L/2-lq+t; y=0; label=2;}    // bottom edge, chip heat flux
border C03(t=0, L/2-lq){x=L/2+lq+t; y=0; label=1;}  // bottom edge, adiabatic right
border C04(t=0, H){x=L; y=t; label=3;}              // right edge, convection
border C05(t=0, L){x=L-t; y=H; label=3;}            // top edge, convection
border C06(t=0, H){x=0; y=H-t; label=3;}            // left edge, convection
int n = 50;
mesh Th = buildmesh(C01(n) + C02(n) + C03(n) + C04(n) + C05(n) + C06(n));
extracted.geometry_description: The design domain is the normalized unit square — the cross-section of an aluminium heat sink scaled to unit size. A power chip occupying the central forty percent of the bottom edge injects a uniform heat flux; the remaining bottom edge is adiabatic and the bottom edge is a fixed boundary. The other three edges exchange heat with ambient air at u_amb = 298 K by convection (h = 25 W/(m^2 K)) and surface radiation (epsilon = 0.8, sigma = 5.67e-8 W/(m^2 K^4)). The initial design is the full solid square with a circular hole of radius 0.1 cut out of its centre.

designed.mesh_code:
real L = 1.0;    // normalized design-domain width
real H = 1.0;    // normalized design-domain height
real lq = 0.2;   // half-length of the chip heat-flux segment (chip = central 40%)
border C01(t=0, L/2-lq){x=t; y=0; label=1;}         // bottom edge, adiabatic left
border C02(t=0, 2*lq){x=L/2-lq+t; y=0; label=2;}    // bottom edge, chip heat flux
border C03(t=0, L/2-lq){x=L/2+lq+t; y=0; label=1;}  // bottom edge, adiabatic right
border C04(t=0, H){x=L; y=t; label=3;}              // right edge, convection
border C05(t=0, L){x=L-t; y=H; label=3;}            // top edge, convection
border C06(t=0, H){x=0; y=H-t; label=3;}            // left edge, convection
int n = 50;
mesh Th = buildmesh(C01(n) + C02(n) + C03(n) + C04(n) + C05(n) + C06(n));
designed.domain_description: Normalized unit square [0,1]x[0,1] representing the cross-section of an aluminium heat sink. The bottom edge is split into three parts: the central 40% segment (label 2) carries the chip heat flux, while the remaining bottom segments (label 1) are adiabatic. The right, top and left edges (label 3) are the cooling boundaries that exchange heat by convection and radiation. The initial circular hole is carved by the level-set function, so no mesh-side hole is required.
